title: Why I Started This Blog
sum: A personal space for sharing what environmental work looks like beyond reports, regulations and project deliverables — shaped by experience across the MENA region.
body:
Welcome.

I’m Mahmoud Khattab, an environmental professional working across environmental assessment, compliance, and project delivery in the Middle East and North Africa.

Over the past several years, I’ve had the opportunity to work across oil and gas, energy, industrial, infrastructure, construction, and recycling projects. My experience has taken me through different stages of project development — from environmental and social impact assessment, scoping and baseline studies to impact evaluation, permitting, auditing, environmental management, and monitoring.

But this blog is not another version of my CV.

It is a place to talk about how environmental work actually works.

Beyond the Report

Environmental work can sometimes look straightforward from the outside: collect the data, assess the impacts, propose mitigation, obtain approval, and move on.

In reality, it rarely works that neatly.

A baseline study can be technically sound and still fail to answer the questions that matter. A mitigation measure can look perfectly reasonable in a report but prove difficult to implement once a project reaches the field. A compliance issue that seems minor at first can become significantly harder — and more expensive — to address when it is discovered late.

These are the parts of environmental practice that are rarely captured in formal deliverables.

They are also some of the most valuable lessons.

Working across different projects and regulatory environments has taught me to look beyond whether something is technically correct on paper and ask a more practical question:

Will this actually work when the project is being built, operated, and managed on the ground?

That question has shaped much of how I approach environmental work today.

What I Want to Explore Here

This blog is where I want to document some of those lessons.

I’ll write about environmental assessment, impact evaluation, baseline studies, compliance, permitting, environmental management, and the practical challenges that come with applying these disciplines to real projects.

I’ll also explore broader topics that increasingly shape the environmental profession — including climate change, waste management, the circular economy, sustainability, and the changing expectations around environmental performance.

Some articles will be technical. Others will be more reflective.

The common thread will be practical experience: what works, what doesn’t, why it matters, and what I’ve learned along the way.

For People Working in the Field — and Those Entering It

One of the things I’ve come to appreciate about environmental work is how much of the profession is learned through experience.

You learn by reviewing a baseline that doesn’t quite answer the right question. By walking a site and noticing something a desktop assessment missed. By trying to implement a mitigation measure that seemed perfectly logical during the planning stage. And sometimes, by making a mistake and making sure you don’t repeat it.

I want this blog to capture some of that practical knowledge.

If you’re already working in environmental consultancy, E&S, HSE, sustainability, or project development, I hope you’ll find ideas that are useful in your own work.

If you’re a student or early-career professional, I hope it gives you a clearer picture of what the profession looks like beyond textbooks and job descriptions.

A Personal Perspective

This is a personal blog, not a company publication.

The experiences and perspectives I share here are my own and are intended for professional discussion, general information, and learning. I will avoid sharing confidential project information or material that could compromise the interests of clients, employers, or project stakeholders.

My goal is not to present environmental work as a perfect process.

It isn't.

The field is constantly evolving, and there is always more to learn.

This blog is simply my way of documenting that journey, sharing what I learn, and contributing to the wider conversation around how environmental considerations can be understood and managed better in real projects.

Thanks for being here.

Welcome to the blog.
